title: ReachAloud: I built a multilingual voice tool that reads emergency alerts aloud for people who can't read the screen
why_read: An accessibility-focused TTS tool for translating emergency alerts into spoken, multilingual audio, a reasonable but narrow application of existing text-to-speech APIs.
analysis: ReachAloud converts text-based emergency alerts into multilingual spoken audio for people who can't read the alert text, addressing a real accessibility gap highlighted by a specific flood disaster example. The technical implementation appears to be a straightforward wrapper around TTS/translation APIs (likely ElevenLabs, given the challenge series) rather than a novel technical contribution. It's a worthwhile use case for accessibility-minded engineers but not deeply technical.
